batch_strategy: Targeted same-family condition and loading response curves for aromatic-basic and amino-nitrile failures, combined with high-tail oxygenated and carbonyl probes for broader residual repair.

choices.reason: Low-strength m141 endpoint at lower loading brackets measured m141 responses at 1/1 and 2/1 in de4e10d3a5d448ffcdda and eceaa4f4139cde7ba166, testing onset before the observed late-retention regime.
The 5/1, low-loading m141 point extends the ratio curve against measured 5/1, high-loading row 65f4f125b5e1f8137bd9 and the 1/1 low-loading anchor 835b5f2641442576de42.
This 10/1 m141 point at low loading tests the steep predicted transition between measured 5/1 and 20/1 high-loading rows 65f4f125b5e1f8137bd9 and 51f4126a3aadb3239225.
Matched to the preceding m141 ratio point but at higher loading, it isolates loading sensitivity at 10/1 and can be compared with measured 10/1 m141 row 6f548d72f01fc85debdc.
A low-ratio, higher-loading m146 anchor tests whether the fused basic-nitrogen effect emerges gradually from measured 1/1 and 2/1 rows 9a58eec5ad3051be568a and cf36dbeee8bb51632d84.
The 1/1, low-loading m146 point supplies a direct loading contrast to measured 1/1 m146 row 9a58eec5ad3051be568a and helps separate the unusually late 5/1 response in 04a2e8ad27ca641a3a12.
A second 1/1 m146 loading level tests whether onset and completion shift together with loading, using measured 9a58eec5ad3051be568a as the same-condition reference.
The 5/1, higher-loading m146 point tests whether measured late 5/1 row 04a2e8ad27ca641a3a12 and extreme 10/1 row 9e3ce3497298084abd83 extrapolate smoothly to another loading.
This low-ratio, higher-loading m216 point tests the lower endpoint of the measured m216 ratio series beginning with ae187d6f3746213b630c and rising through e7bf6bd74f8498f1cb11.
The 5/1, low-loading m216 experiment gives a loading contrast to measured 5/1 m216 row 33ffc69a253a89f15995, whose late onset and tail remain difficult to interpolate.
The 10/1, high-loading m216 point tests the upper end of the observed m216 ratio response against measured 10/1 row 9cd02352c2ed7a3e2321.
Pyridyl ester m90 at 10/1 and moderate loading probes a basic ester family adjacent to m66 and extends measured m90 anchors 0460dfc4e1747f0fc92c and 9a9b50816ec47f1cd755 into a high-width region.

A strong-eluent, high-loading m211 point extends the measured m211 condition series represented by 292e0342682192a69fce, d119d77f545c029deace, and 434e465cfa7e0034f233 into a new tail regime.
The 1/1 m160 amino-nitrile point tests the low-ratio side of the positional response against measured para-isomer rows 2feb7d8e0a3566ddf97f and b4e0e9dc92fca2c88b90.
Low-loading m160 at 5/1 provides a direct amount contrast to measured 5/1 m160 row b4e0e9dc92fca2c88b90 and the matched higher-loading candidate, targeting the large amino-nitrile tail uncertainty.
The higher-loading 5/1 m160 point completes a loading-response pair around measured late row b4e0e9dc92fca2c88b90 and can teach onset versus completion scaling separately.
The 0/1 meta-isomer m161 anchor tests whether positional effects persist at weak elution relative to measured 1/1 m161 row 0c24b9414856413c9a67.
Low-loading 5/1 m161 is a positional and loading contrast to measured 5/1 m161 row 17902fa9c7f8ea9b456e, whose completion volume is substantially late.
The 1/1, higher-loading m161 point tests whether the meta-isomer onset and tail change smoothly from measured 1/1 row 0c24b9414856413c9a67.
High-width m107 at 5/1 and lower loading is a loading contrast to measured 5/1 m107 row 2cfa393cb79664e100ce and tests a carbonyl-rich tail without assuming a universal V2 shift.
The 20/1 m82 point at lower loading directly contrasts measured high-loading m82 row b6bf451b4911ee22d4a4 and probes whether the large tail is amount-dependent.
Strong-eluent m11 with a new loading level probes a high-width oxygenated oxime-like row and can distinguish a smooth condition response from heterogeneous carbonyl-rich outcomes.
The high-ratio m117 point targets a broad predicted V1/V2 region and extends measured m117 anchors 09c2a4beb05ca5c84aab and cac9ff0c40665baf313f into an untested condition.
The 5/1 m94 high-loading point tests carbonyl-tail topology against measured m94 rows 4dedc80fb33d21596b7e and 5b445b457a8b897a2d6c, which show different completion behavior.
A moderate-loading 10/1 m95 point probes whether the extreme measured m95 completion behavior in 5fd0921bbbba1e22abf9 is localized to loading or generalizes across conditions.
The low-loading 5/1 m13 point gives a matched contrast to measured 5/1 m13 row 5d530b2f228ed39ff952 and the very late 10/1 row 9e3e08d6bc42e91e2679.
This PE-loaded m20 condition probes a donor-free multi-acceptor tail at 10/1, complementing measured 5/1 m20 outcome c86b03e1b275528444a6 and testing solvent-strength transfer.

hypotheses.content: Aromatic-basic and fused-ring nitrogen compounds show nonlinear, structure-specific retention with PE/EA and loading; onset and completion can shift late together.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The largest known errors are concentrated in this region, while descriptor-similar basic rows do not share a simple correction. Matched condition curves can teach graph-condition interactions and V2 tails that interpolation currently misses.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do these late responses rise smoothly with solvent strength and loading, or do fused topology and nitrogen accessibility create separate response regimes?

hypotheses.content: Positional amino-nitrile isomers retain very differently despite matching coarse descriptors, with additional interactions from PE/EA and loading.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: These rows expose limitations of count-based descriptors and can improve local positional encoding, onset/tail coupling, and transfer to other substituted aromatic nitrogen compounds.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Can the graph representation learn the positional difference consistently across loading and solvent-strength contrasts?

hypotheses.content: Oxygenated and carbonyl-rich V2 tails are heterogeneous and condition-specific; a global tail correction would damage generalization.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Observed V2 errors have both signs and vary by topology, loading, and condition. New matched tail probes should help the retrained model learn when broadening is structural rather than calibration noise.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Which combinations of carbonyl topology, donor status, loading amount, and eluent strength predict a long completion tail?

hypotheses.content: Loading amount interacts with solvent strength for high-polarity donor and acceptor systems, so amount contrasts are needed to separate loading effects from structural retention.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The same nominal molecule families show large changes with loading and condition, and the current predictor often misses V2 more than V1. Matched amount pairs can improve interaction terms that generalize across polar molecules.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Are the observed loading effects smooth and transferable, or do they depend on specific donor/acceptor arrangements and loading solvent?

feedback_interpretation: Recent outcomes weakened any blanket correction for polar or oxygenated structures. The amino ester f6cfe706d71f58273c59 and alcohol 56f8cdbb3999b366d947 were both overpredicted, while m74 0b9226171e1caa865abb and trifluoroethyl acrylate 6cfbe3ab4c27733a07b6 showed different V2 failure directions. The sulfur and donor-free anchors were comparatively stable. I therefore concentrated the new batch on unresolved aromatic-basic and amino-nitrile response curves, while retaining selected high-width carbonyl, donor, and loading contrasts to learn when tails broaden rather than applying a global correction.
batch_rationale: The batch repairs the dominant measured failure region with dense but interpretable local curves: m141, m146, m216, m90, and the amino-nitrile positional pair are sampled across PE/EA and loading. Several choices are matched amount or condition contrasts, so their labels can identify onset versus completion sensitivity and distinguish smooth response from topology-specific jumps. The remaining choices target high-width m107, m82, m11, m117, m94, m95, m13, m20, m114, m204, m206, and m45 rows. These preserve coverage of oxygenated, carbonyl-rich, donor-containing, and acidic systems where recent feedback showed signed V2 errors in both directions. Together the batch combines failure repair, hypothesis discrimination, and broader functional-group coverage, which should improve learned structure-condition interactions and generalization across the Row-distribution.
